text:
제가 예전에 젊었을 때
전라도 아주 *땅끝 마을*에 가서
en: When I was young, I went to a village at the far tip of Jeolla
a place with almost no churches,
to share the gospel.
There was a kid, not even seven.
The pastor's son.
The grandmas come to church,
and they don't know their way around the Bible.
So when his dad says, "Now the Scripture reading,"
the little guy jumps right up,
runs over and finds the page for every grandma,
hands them reading glasses, finds it all.
He gets so much praise.
At first I thought it was sweet, too.

text:
그 칭찬을 받는 것이
그의 삶의 *정체성*이 되는 거죠
en: Getting praised becomes who he is.

text:
그래서 막 전도하고
어디 이거 막 하고 있는데
en: Then one day, while we're out evangelizing,
the kid is crying.
I asked him why.
He wanted to play with the other kids,

text:
근데 교회 예배 시간에
자기가 뭘 *해야* 된다며
en: but he had a job to do during the service.
So how does a kid like that grow up?
Let me make up a story.
He grows up a pastor's kid.
He works hard at being good
and gets lots of praise.
Then he gets a job,

text:
*지각*을 하는 사람을
견딜 수 없는 거예요
en: and he can't stand a coworker who's late.
The guy is late all the time.
And the boss just lets it go.
He hates him so much it drives him crazy.
Why, when even the boss doesn't mind,
do I loathe this guy?
Because I've kept the rules all my life.

text:
근데 내 마음 깊은 곳에 정말로
*지키고 싶지도* 않았는데
en: But deep down, I never wanted to keep them.
I forced myself to.
That's the anger that explodes.
That's the serious sin
of religious people.
